skill.name: kubernetes-triage-expert
skill.description:
Analyze Kubernetes faults using only user-provided evidence. Classify the fault,
rank likely hypotheses, request the next highest-value checks, and keep facts
separate from guesses. Do not execute commands, inspect systems, call tools,
or claim environment visibility.
skill.summary: Triage Kubernetes incidents from supplied evidence, rank hypotheses, and recommend targeted checks without accessing the cluster.
skill.author: ghostwritten

security_audit.summary: All 165 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, sample identifiers, installation instructions, diagnostic prose, or readable Chinese text. No evidence found of malicious execution, credential exfiltration, or audit-directed prompt injection. One separate disclosure risk remains: examples request full deployment manifests without redaction guidance.

remediation.issue: The examples request complete deployment YAML in chat without warning that manifests can contain sensitive values.
remediation.suggestion: In both example documents, request only relevant RBAC, image, and configuration-reference fields. Require redaction of credentials, tokens, literal environment values, and sensitive annotations.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes incident reports often lack enough evidence to identify the next useful check. This skill separates facts from hypotheses and recommends focused checks without claiming cluster access.
actual_capabilities: Normalize incident reports into affected objects, symptoms, timing, impact, recent changes, and strongest evidence.
Classify startup, scheduling, networking, storage, resource, and rollout failures from supplied evidence.
Rank up to three hypotheses using evidence fit, recent changes, common causes, and diagnostic value.
Recommend up to three checks with a purpose and alternative result interpretations.
Review suspected causes and separate confirmed facts, likely causes, excluded paths, and missing evidence.
Prepare specialist handoffs when evidence points beyond Kubernetes triage.
limitations: No commands, telemetry collection, cluster inspection, or remediation are performed.
Conclusions depend on the accuracy and completeness of user-provided evidence.
Application internals, node runtimes, storage backends, and cloud internals require specialist investigation.
Behavioral restrictions are prompt instructions, not technical access controls; redact sensitive evidence before sharing.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Incident Checks
use_cases.description: Turn a production alert, timeline, and selected error lines into a short list of evidence-backed hypotheses and next checks.

use_cases.title: Investigate Release Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare symptoms before and after a rollout to identify configuration, image, probe, or resource changes worth checking.

use_cases.title: Review Operational AI Responses
use_cases.description: Use the included examples, stress tests, and review templates to assess evidence discipline, diagnostic usefulness, and scope boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Clarify a Pod Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use kubernetes-triage-expert. My Pod is not starting, and I only know its namespace is [namespace]. Ask up to three questions that distinguish the failure stage. Do not assume a root cause or access the cluster.
prompt_templates.scenario: Initial intake when evidence is limited.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Review Missing Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use kubernetes-triage-expert. Deployment [name] in [namespace] began failing after rollout [time]. The supplied status is CrashLoopBackOff, and the log says missing REDIS_URL. Rank up to three hypotheses and recommend targeted checks. Request configuration references and key names, not secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compare Conflicting Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use kubernetes-triage-expert. Service [name] has no endpoints, but the supplied Pod statuses are Ready. Redacted selectors, labels, and namespaces: [evidence]. Review the evidence, distinguish confirmed facts from hypotheses, and recommend up to three checks. Explain how each possible result changes the diagnosis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Service diagnosis with apparently conflicting health signals.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Challenge a Root-Cause Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Use kubernetes-triage-expert to review the proposed cause [claim]. Timeline: [timeline]. Evidence before the change: [redacted evidence]. Evidence after the change: [redacted evidence]. Existing rollback observations: [observations]. Identify contradictions and missing evidence. Rank only supported hypotheses and prepare a specialist handoff if the strongest evidence exceeds Kubernetes triage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evidence review across multiple investigation turns.

output_examples.input: A user reports that a Pod is not starting but provides no status or error.
output: Assessment: The failure stage and severity are not yet established.
Confirmed: A workload is reported unhealthy.
Next checks: Provide the workload identity and status, the incident timeline, and one relevant redacted event or error line.
Conclusion: Evidence is insufficient to confirm a cause.

output_examples.input: A deployment started crash-looping after a rollout, and the supplied startup log reports missing REDIS_URL.
output: Assessment: Startup configuration failure associated with a rollout.
Confirmed: The supplied log reports missing configuration.
Leading hypotheses: A configuration source changed, a referenced key is missing, or the new application version expects additional configuration.
Next check: Compare old and new configuration references and key names without sharing values.
Interpretation: A changed reference supports a release configuration regression; unchanged references leave application expectations or configuration loading unresolved.
Conclusion: The error is established, but its exact configuration cause still needs evidence.

output_examples.input: The supplied evidence shows a Running Pod, healthy readiness, HTTP 500 responses, and a SQL syntax error.
output: Assessment: The strongest evidence points to application or database behavior.
Confirmed: The supplied status and readiness evidence do not explain the SQL error.
Next check: Review the failing query context and relevant application changes with sensitive values removed.
Handoff: Application or database owners should continue the investigation.
Conclusion: A Kubernetes root cause is not established.

best_practices: Provide the workload identity, incident timing, recent changes, and a short exact error excerpt.
Redact tokens, credentials, connection values, and sensitive annotations; share configuration references and key names instead.
Review proposed checks before running them, and return targeted results so hypotheses can be updated.
anti_patterns: Treating a status label such as CrashLoopBackOff as proof of a particular root cause.
Expecting the skill to inspect the cluster, execute commands, or apply fixes.
Sharing complete manifests or logs containing credentials when selected redacted fields would answer the diagnostic question.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a fault classification, confirmed facts, up to three hypotheses, targeted next checks, and a qualified conclusion.

faq.question: Can it run kubectl or change the cluster?
faq.answer: No. The skill prohibits command execution and remediation. Operators collect evidence and decide whether to make changes.

faq.question: What evidence should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the namespace, workload identity, symptom, start time, affected scope, recent changes, and selected redacted events or log excerpts.

faq.question: Will it always identify the root cause?
faq.answer: No. It should state when evidence is insufficient and request checks that distinguish the remaining hypotheses.

faq.question: Which output language does it use?
faq.answer: It follows your current language and defaults to Chinese when the language is unclear. Technical identifiers remain unchanged.

faq.question: Is it safe to paste full manifests or Secret values?
faq.answer: Do not share Secret values, tokens, or credentials. Redact sensitive fields and provide only the evidence needed for the current check.
